interest: This file is historically valuable because it captures the practical legal realities and diplomatic complexities surrounding American real property ownership in Japan during the interwar period. It highlights how private citizens, legal practitioners, and state officials navigated conflicting legal traditions regarding probate, testamentary devises, and alien land legislation following Japan's 1925 Alien Land Law. Furthermore, the record documents the winding down of foreign perpetual leases, lists notable American landholders in Japan including prominent architect Antonin Raymond, and illustrates domestic economic frictions over Japanese commercial real estate purchases in Hawaii.
overview: This file consists of the Department of State's List of Papers (docket and purport sheets, Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.5211, titled 'Right Of Nationals Of United States To Hold Or Acquire Real Property In Japan,' covering communications and cross-references between 1929 and 1939 with record entries through 1945. The documents indexed in the file address legal and diplomatic inquiries regarding the acquisition, ownership, lease, and testamentary disposition of real estate in Japan by American citizens. Prominent topics include the administration and probate of foreign estates under Japanese law (such as the estate of Irene Mann and an inheritance query by attorney Isaac A. Pennypacker), the winding up of perpetual leases by foreigners in Japan in coordination with the British, Far Eastern Division memoranda identifying American landholders in Japan, interpretations of residential and commercial leasing rights under the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, and labor protests by the Metal Trade Council of Hawaii against the establishment of a Mitsukoshi Department Store branch in Honolulu.

subfiles.about: Department of State List of Papers indexing correspondence, memoranda, and cross-reference sheets concerning the rights of American nationals to hold, acquire, inherit, and lease real property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This three-page Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46 docket sheet) for decimal file 894.5211 indexes records from 1929 to 1939 regarding American real property rights in Japan. Key indexed items include legal inquiries by private citizens and state officials concerning Japanese inheritance and probate laws, Far Eastern Division memoranda analyzing foreign estate settlement procedures, and a list of American citizens owning land in Japan. The sheets also record cross-references regarding Anglo-American cooperation on ending perpetual leases, treaty provisions governing commercial and residential leases, and a labor protest against a Japanese department store acquiring real estate in Honolulu.
